title: ReChisel: Effective Automatic Chisel Code Generation by LLM with Reflection
problem: Chisel (high-level HDL based on Scala) enables more concise and maintainable hardware designs than Verilog, but LLM-based Chisel code generation remains unexplored despite growing interest in LLM-assisted HDL coding.
motivation: Hardware design productivity is critical; Chisel's high-level abstractions provide benefits over traditional Verilog, but lack of LLM tools for Chisel limits adoption and automation opportunities.
method: ReChisel starts by having an AI write code in Chisel, a programming language designed specifically for describing hardware circuits. The generated code is then tested using a compiler and simulator (tools that check if the code works), and any errors or failures are reported back to the AI. The AI takes this feedback and rewrites the code to fix what went wrong, then the cycle repeats—test the new code, get feedback, improve the code. The system keeps doing this until the code works correctly, and it includes a mechanism to escape if it gets stuck repeating the same failed attempts.
key_novelty: For the first time, an AI system can automatically generate Chisel hardware code by iteratively refining its output based on feedback from compiler and simulator tests.
contributions: ReChisel: First LLM-based system for Chisel code generation
Escape mechanism to break non-progress loops
Success rate comparable to state-of-the-art Verilog LLM-based systems
Demonstrated effectiveness of iterative refinement for HDL generation
